Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Third Quarter 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust net written premium growth across our lines of business, favorable reserve development trends, solid reinsurance recoveries both received and anticipated, and improving loss ratio trends reflecting better claims frequency and severity management.

David, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Thompson: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $2.15 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included top-line expansion from net written premiums and favorable reserve releases that bolstered the bottom line. Our combined ratio was 92.5%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with $15 billion in statutory surplus and a risk-based capital ratio of 320%.

Let me start with our top-line growth, a key highlight this quarter. Net written premiums, or NWP, grew 8.7% year-over-year to $12.4 billion. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-cat growth and reflects disciplined pricing, strong retention rates, and targeted new business wins across our diversified portfolio.

Personal Lines, which represent 42% of our total NWP, grew 7.2% to $5.2 billion. Personal Auto delivered solid 6.5% growth to $3.1 billion, fueled by a 4.2-point rate increase amid ongoing supply chain pressures on repair costs and medical inflation at 5.8%, aligning with Verisk Analytics benchmarks. Retention held steady at 88.5%, up 50 basis points year-over-year, thanks to our ApexDrive telematics program now covering over 2.2 million policyholders. This usage-based insurance has improved risk selection by 15%, reducing our loss ratio by 2.1 points in the quarter. Homeowners and other personal lines were up 9.1% to $2.1 billion, benefiting from California wildfire repricing with 7.8% rate adequacy and expansion in Florida post-Hurricane Ian, growing policies 12% through independent agent partnerships. U.S. Personal Lines drove 85% of this growth, with early traction in our UK personal motor adding $150 million amid Brexit-related market shifts.

Commercial Lines, our fastest-growing segment at 12.4% NWP expansion to $4.1 billion or 33% of total, capitalized on a hardening market with average rate gains of 8.9%, comparable to peers like Travelers and The Hartford. Middle-market commercial P&C surged 11.8% to $2.9 billion, with key wins from our ApexGuard SME package bundling cyber riders, attracting 25,000 new accounts year-to-date. Large corporate grew 14.2% to $1.2 billion via disciplined underwriting in excess and surplus lines, exiting 15% of underperforming construction and manufacturing books to focus on high-margin tech and renewables sectors where social inflation has moderated to 4.2% per our models. Europe contributed 22% of commercial growth, particularly Germany D&O amid economic uncertainty, while Asia-Pacific added via our Singapore hub up 18% in logistics and marine cargo.

Specialty Lines shone with 15.2% NWP growth to $2.3 billion, now 19% of our book. Cyber insurance led at 22.4% to $950 million, capturing 30% EMEA market share post-MOVEit breaches via our Silent Cyber program with parametric triggers. D&O rose 13.7% on 9.2% rate hikes and our AI underwriting platform cutting cycle times 40% and improving attritional loss ratios to 58%. Environmental and trade credit posted double-digits, with Australia wildfire parametrics up 28% and LatAm credit insurance growing 16% amid Argentina volatility. Our Helix AI models enhance predictive analytics, pricing 95% of risks within 1% of ultimate loss.

Life and Group Benefits, at 6% of NWP, grew a modest 4.3% to $820 million. Universal life and annuities up 5.1% on higher crediting rates from Fed hikes, while group health faced 6.2% medical trends offset by our ApexWellness app boosting retention to 92%. We're de-risking with 25% more term life ceded to Swiss Re.

Organic growth was 7.9%, with 0.8 points from last year's Nordic Specialty acquisition. Retention averaged 89.2% company-wide, new business $1.2 billion at mid-90s combined ratios. We expect 8-10% NWP growth in FY23, supported by 5-7% pricing, telematics to 30% auto penetration, and $200 million capex for digital distribution via embedded insurance APIs akin to Lemonade or Progressive tech. Amid cat losses 20% above PCS average, our ex-cat loss ratio improved 1.8 points to 61.2%. Portfolio optimization prioritizes high-growth, low-vol lines like cyber and parametric.

Turning to our core P&C metrics, loss ratios came in at 91.8% for the quarter—our best in over two years and a 340 basis point improvement year-over-year from 95.2%. Excluding catastrophes, the underlying loss ratio improved to 87.4%, down 280 bps. This reflects multi-year pricing and underwriting discipline across Personal and Commercial segments.

Claims frequency remains stable to improving. In Personal Auto—45% of net earned premiums—frequency declined 3.2% year-over-year via our DriveSafe app at 28% penetration, up from 18%, mirroring Progressive's 2-4% reductions. Homeowners frequency flat at 1.12 claims per $100 exposure via AI risk models avoiding litigious states. Commercial Workers' Comp up 1.8% from return-to-work delays, offset by 4.1% General Liability drop from subcontractor underwriting. Overall ex-cat frequency down 1.5%, per ISO/Verisk.

Severity up 4.7% to $18,400 per claim from repair/medical inflation/litigation. Auto physical damage +6.2% with $2,100 body shop bills; medical 5.8% with double-digit MRI/PT in no-fault states. Property +3.1% from wind/hail; countered by GLMs improving rate adequacy 15%, Xactimate pilots cutting severity 2%.

Cats hit $450 million or 4.2 points—above 3-point target but below PCS industry $1.1 billion. Helene/Milton 60%, Southeast homeowners trimmed 8% YoY. Europe 0.5 points from Storm Boris. Favorable prior-year development added 1.8 points benefit, $220 million year-to-date.

Regionally: U.S. (72%) Personal at 93.2%, improving 450 bps, Gulf at 102% with 12.4% hikes. Europe (18%) 84.6%, motor via LexisNexis fraud cuts. Asia-Pac (10%) 89.1%, Thailand floods 1.2 points, micro-insurance sub-85%. LatAm 86% with Brazil telematics.

Precision Underwriting 3.0 validates: 9.8% rates via 150+ GLM factors; RPA bots 35% first-notice, LAE to 12.4%; quota-share drops 2 points ceded, $15 billion cat protection as RMS losses rise 20%; mix to captives/cyber at 82% ratios.

Full-year ex-cat guide 88-89%, Q4 holiday/telematics benefits; long-term mid-80s by 2026, ROE 14%+.

Reserve development continues as a bright spot in P&C underwriting. It reflects differences between original loss reserve estimates for prior accident years and actual ultimate losses as claims mature. Favorable development releases capital when actuals are below provisions; unfavorable pressures margins.

Q3 was highly favorable at $285 million pre-tax, 18% bottom-line contribution, strongest quarterly in five years. Year-to-date $1.05 billion, up 22% from $860 million prior year. Calendar-year 4.2% of net earned premiums, ahead of 2.8% long-term average and peers Travelers (3.1%), Chubb (2.9%).

By segment: P&C Commercial $190 million from 2021-2022 years. AI catastrophe modeling with RMS v18.1/AIR refined post-Ian/Ida PMLs, 5.2-point ultimate loss ratio improvement in E&S property to 58% vs. 63% original/IBNR. Rebuild inflation moderated with supply chains, parametric triggers in 40% new policies.

Personal Auto/Homeowners $65 million: auto physical damage repair inflation peaked 15% YoY 2022, now 8%; telematics 2.5 million policies with Cambridge Mobile Telematics cut tail IBNR 12%. Homeowners wildfire sub-limits better in California via drone inspections accelerating 35%.

Workers' Comp/Specialty $15 million unfavorable (0.3% premiums), California 2019-2020 comp from Medicare audits/opioid litigation like CNA/Hartford; offset by D&O releases with cyber exclusions/manuscripts.

U.S. 72% favorability from 9.2% renewal rates, E&S softening. Europe $45 million, UK motor post-Brexit, IFRS 17 sharpening. Asia-Pac -$5 million Thailand floods, protected by Swiss Re/Munich Re 1:3 transfer.

Reserving robust: ML for LDFs with Verisk/ISO data; Bornhuetter-Ferguson IBNR Bayesian-refined, 92% back-test accuracy; sensitivities for 200bps rates/5% inflation.

Disciplined selection: non-renewed $400 million middle-market casualty, grew habitational E&S 15%. 2024 reinsurance 45% cession U.S. property cat at 120% attachment.

Full-year $1.3-1.5 billion favorable, Q4 auto seasonality strong. Risks: 6% social inflation (NCCI), convective storms. $12.5 billion surplus, 250% CR resilience; 75% releases to buybacks/dividends.

On reinsurance recoveries, critical for loss dynamics/earnings stability. Our program blends quota share on property cat and excess-of-loss above $100 million retentions with Swiss Re, Munich Re, Berkshire Hathaway.

Q3 we recognized $285 million received, 28% YoY up from $222 million; year-to-date $512 million, +32%. Added 15 bps to combined ratio at 92.4%, strongest in three quarters.

65% or $185 million cat: $120 million proportional on Hurricane Beryl Florida via 40% Swiss Re quota. Non-cat $100 million U.S. workers' comp/international liability from 2022 California wildfire IBNR.

North America 72%, Beryl $450 million gross, 60% net recovery post-reinstatements. Europe 18%/$51 million Q3 Germany floods via Munich Re, drone verification. Asia-Pac 8%/$23 million Typhoon Gaemi, monitoring Japan cat bond.

Trends: AI analytics with Verisk Touchstone cut recovery lag 180 to 120 days, ceded recoverables to 18% gross reserves from 22%. Hardening markets: Jan 1 5% lower ceding commissions, A+ security.

Year-to-date 12% above guidance, Maui subrogation $35 million via Sedgwick.

Expected: $620 million next 12 months, $410 million H2; $280 million 2024 cats (Beryl tail $150 million, Europe storms), $220 million priors ($90 million Ian retro with RenaissanceRe). 95% collectible, 85% collateralized; RMS v18 stress-tested.

Innovation: parametric flood swaps with Aon $15 million auto post-Beryl. 2025 renewal targets 10-15% cost cut via Everest Re cat bonds, reinsurance expense 25% gross premiums for mid-teens ROE in 1-in-50 cat year.

Full-year $1.1 billion, 8% above consensus. On track.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the reserve development trends, particularly how you're thinking about the Workers' Comp unfavorable piece?

David Thompson: Good morning, Emily. The $15 million unfavorable in Workers' Comp was isolated to long-tail California claims from 2019-2020, driven by Medicare set-aside audits and opioid litigation trends we've seen across the industry. It was more than offset elsewhere, and our overall reserving process—with ML models and Bayesian refinements—maintains high accuracy. We're comfortable with the full-year outlook.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent catastrophe activity on your reinsurance recoveries and loss ratios?

Michael Reynolds: Thanks, Robert. The cats like Helene, Milton, and Beryl were significant, but our program delivered—$285 million Q3 recoveries, with strong cessions mitigating the $450 million hit to just 4.2 loss ratio points. Expected pipeline remains robust at $620 million, supporting stability.

David Thompson: To add, our accelerated billing and parametric innovations have kept lags short and collectibility high.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: Hi, team. On NWP growth, how sustainable is the specialty lines momentum, especially cyber?

Lisa Chen: Hi, Lisa. Cyber's 22.4% growth is demand-driven post-breaches, with our AI platform ensuring 58% attritional ratios. We're expanding parametrics and E&S selectively, targeting continued double-digits without chasing volume.

Operator: Our next question from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. What's your view on loss ratio drivers into next year, severity headwinds?

David Thompson: Severity at 4.7% remains a focus—inflation in repairs and medical—but GLMs and telematics are countering effectively. Guide to 88-89% ex-cat full-year, trending mid-80s long-term as inflation eases to 3%.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
